title: DLGAP5 Regulates the Proliferation, Migration, Invasion, and Cell Cycle of Breast Cancer Cells via the JAK2/STAT3 Signaling Axis.
authors: Li, Yujie; Wei, Jie; Sun, Yao; Zhou, Wenqian; Ma, Xiaoya; Guo, Jinping; Zhang, Huan; Jin, Tianbo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究乳腺癌中DLGAP5通过JAK2/STAT3信号轴调控细胞增殖迁移，属纯细胞与信号通路实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The aim of this study was to discover new biomarkers to detect breast cancer (BC), which is an aggressive cancer with a high mortality rate. In this study, bioinformatic analyses (differential analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine learning) were performed to identify potential candidate genes for BC to study their molecular mechanisms. Furthermore, Quantitative Real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry assays were used to examine the protein and mRNA expression levels of a particular candidate gene (DLGAP5). And the effects of DLGAP5 on cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and cell cycle were further assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, colony formation, Transwell, wound healing, and flow cytometry assays. Moreover, the changes in the JAK2/STAT3 signaling-pathway-related proteins were detected by Western Blot. A total of 44 overlapping genes were obtained by differential analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, of which 25 genes were found in the most tightly connected cluster. Finally, NEK2, CKS2, UHRF1, DLGAP5, and FAM83D were considered as potential biomarkers of BC. Moreover, DLGAP5 was highly expressed in BC. The down-regulation of DLGAP5 may inhibit the proliferation, migration, invasion, and cell cycle of BC cells, and the opposite was true for DLGAP5 overexpression. Correspondingly, silencing or overexpression of the DLGAP5 gene inhibited or activated the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway, respectively. DLGAP5, as a potential biomarker of BC, may impact the cell proliferation, migration, invasion, cell cycle, and BC development by modulating the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在发现新的生物标志物以检测乳腺癌（breast cancer, BC），这是一种具有高死亡率的侵袭性癌症。在本研究中，进行了生物信息学分析（差异分析、加权基因共表达网络分析和机器学习），以识别BC的潜在候选基因并研究其分子机制。此外，使用实时定量PCR和免疫组织化学检测特定候选基因（DLGAP5）的蛋白质和mRNA表达水平。并通过细胞计数试剂盒-8实验、集落形成、Transwell、伤口愈合和流式细胞术进一步评估DLGAP5对细胞增殖、迁移、侵袭和细胞周期的影响。此外，通过Western Blot检测JAK2/STAT3信号通路相关蛋白的变化。通过差异分析和加权基因共表达网络分析共获得44个重叠基因，其中25个基因位于最紧密连接的簇中。最终，NEK2、CKS2、UHRF1、DLGAP5和FAM83D被认为是BC的潜在生物标志物。此外，DLGAP5在BC中高表达。DLGAP5的下调可能抑制BC细胞的增殖、迁移、侵袭和细胞周期，而DLGAP5过表达则相反。相应地，沉默或过表达DLGAP5基因分别抑制或激活JAK2/STAT3信号通路。DLGAP5作为BC的潜在生物标志物，可能通过调节JAK2/STAT3信号通路影响细胞增殖、迁移、侵袭、细胞周期及BC的发展。
